source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Sweet potato, cassava, taro, wild taro, yam, and sago can all substitute for the pumpkin portion of a ration — they're reasonable carbohydrate sources but lower in protein than pumpkin or rice bran, so growth will be somewhat slower, though this can still be a worthwhile trade-off depending on what's available and its price. If dried fish is too expensive at the recommended 5% of the diet, using half that amount (2.5%) still adds meaningfully more protein than leaving it out entirely. Tofu waste can replace dried fish or snails — because it holds a lot of moisture, feed it at the same quantity recommended for fresh snails.
caveat: This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
